findings.text: non-blocking: the assertion is not independent of the value it guards — reckon/crew/picker/client.py:60 builds the request body from JEV_MODEL and the test compares that body against client.JEV_MODEL — so reverting the constant to "typesafe/jev-1.13" leaves it green, and the recorded negative control mutates ask to send a literal (a different regression) instead of reinstating the one the change exists to prevent; folding means one test refusing a pinned release id under reckon/.

non-blocking: the probe script pins JEV_MODEL = "typesafe/jev-1.13" independently of reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9, so after this change the picker tracks the latest alias while the probe keeps measuring an old release; it is outside the node's granted write paths and needs its own node to import the constant or drop its copy.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit — 80ed036c45 changes the JEV_MODEL literal at reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9, and e31770935c replaces a hardcoded request-body literal with client.JEV_MODEL at tests/test_picker.py:377; nothing else is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: all four clauses are measurable and measured — live-call-gate.log records HTTP 200 served model typesafe/jev-1.14-20261014 and the 400 for the tilde-less id, tests-base.log and tests-head.log each read `59 passed ... EXIT=0`, ruff.log reads `All checks passed` and `2 files already formatted`; only the "grep of reckon/ finds no other jev-1.1 model id" clause is claimed in the manifest's artifacts with no grep log on disk, and I reproduced it in the tree myself.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is "JEV_MODEL in reckon/crew/picker/client.py becomes the latest-tracking alias"; reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9 reads JEV_MODEL = "~typesafe/jev-latest" and a grep for jev-1.1 over reckon/ returns nothing, so the deliverable is met in the file the goal names.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at status complete; it names commits 80ed036c45 and e31770935c, the head/base revision pair, two attributed retry_failures, and corrects the brief's claim that tests/test_picker.py:377 was an answering-model fixture when it is the expected request body.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/crew/picker/client.py and tests/test_picker.py; `git diff --stat` over e9805b3a4c..e31770935c shows exactly those two files with 2 insertions and 2 deletions and no other path.

justifications.durability: tests/test_picker.py:377 asserts the posted body against client.JEV_MODEL, the same constant reckon/crew/picker/client.py:60 builds the body from, so restoring the pinned id leaves the assertion green and no test in the repository mentions jev-1 or jev-latest at all.
justifications.evidence: live-call-gate.log and the two suite logs carry revision, tree and command headers and a trailing EXIT= line, but the done_when's grep clause has no gate log and is supported only by the manifest's artifacts line.
justifications.fit: the new assertion at tests/test_picker.py:377 follows the module constant while its neighbours in the same test hardcode wire literals such as the URL and the 10-second timeout, so the changed line reads unlike the assertions beside it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9 carries "~typesafe/jev-latest" and no jev-1.1 id remains under reckon/, but scripts/jev_probe.py:19 still pins the old release id so the repository as a whole still holds a Jev version in two places.
justifications.reuse: no new definition is added, but the capability "one place names the Jev model" already has a fork at scripts/jev_probe.py:19 which this change leaves stale rather than routing to reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff e9805b3a4c..e31770935c touches only reckon/crew/picker/client.py:9 and tests/test_picker.py:377, the two granted paths, one line each.
